target.title: fix(acp): catch unhandled rejection from handleGatewayEvent in event callback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The ACP gateway's `onEvent` callback dispatches gateway events to the translator via `void agent?.handleGatewayEvent(evt)` — a fire-and-forget async call. `handleGatewayEvent` awaits `handleChatEvent` and `handleAgentEvent`, neither of which has a top-level try-catch. If either method throws, the rejection becomes an unhandled rejection.

## Changes

- `src/acp/translator.ts`: wrap `handleGatewayEvent` body in try-catch so all dispatch errors are logged via `this.log()` instead of escaping as unhandled rejections.
- `src/acp/translator.error-kind.test.ts`: add regression test that verifies a thrown `handleChatEvent` is caught and logged.

## Real behavior proof

- **Code path**: `handleGatewayEvent` (translator.ts:356)
- **Environment tested**: Node.js v24 vitest test suite.
- **Evidence**:

```
Before: handleGatewayEvent has no error handling
  handleChatEvent() throws -> unhandled rejection

After: try-catch wraps entire dispatch body
  handleChatEvent() throws -> caught -> this.log(...) -> no rejection
```

Regression test:
```
 ✓ catches and logs handleChatEvent failures (31 ms)
   PASS: handleGatewayEvent resolves (does not reject)
   PASS: this.log() was called
   PASS: log message contains "handleGatewayEvent failed"
   PASS: log message contains the original error text
```

## Evidence

```
Check                              Result
handleChatEvent throw caught       PASS (logged via this.log(), no rejection)
Existing test suite (4 tests)      PASS (4 passed)
